notes: Sources: 2022 UP/UK election result articles (2022 Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly election, 2022 Uttarakhand Legislative Assembly election) for base results; current-members tables embedded in the live 'Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly' and 'Uttarakhand Legislative Assembly' Wikipedia articles (which are maintained with in-place by-election/death/defection updates) used as the primary current-state source, cross-checked against the UP bypoll history table for since-dates; UP MLC from 'List of members of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council' (full historical roll, filtered to terms active on 2026-09-25). UP Assembly: 5 vacancies as of this snapshot (Faridpur (SC), Nizamabad, Ghosi, Rasara, Duddhi (ST) — Duddhi's June 2024 by-election winner Vijay Singh (SP) died 8 Jan 2026 per the article's own remarks column; other 4 are pending by-elections not yet held as of 2026-09-25, could not find WebSearch confirmation this session (WebSearch quota was exhausted session-wide) — dates for these should be re-verified next session). UP MLC: 1 nominated (Governor) seat vacant, could not identify which specific nominee slot from the roll; 'MLA', GR/TA/LA constituency category labels used verbatim from source (GR=Graduates, TA=Teachers, LA=Local Authorities). UK Assembly: fully filled, 70/70, 5 by-elections since 2022 all reflected in current members table (Champawat/Bageshwar/Badrinath/Manglaur/Kedarnath). Party abbreviations: AD(S)=Apna Dal (Sonelal), AD(K)=Apna Dal (Kamerawadi), JD(L)=Jansatta Dal (Loktantrik), SBSP=Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party. Individual MLA/MLC Wikipedia URLs taken directly from the wikilinks in the source tables (not independently verified one by one); ~1 UP MLA (Rahul Lodhi) and 49 UP MLCs have no Wikipedia page and so carry no 'wikipedia' field. This segment does NOT include the 'state_chamber' vs 'state_legislature' kind conflict: a prior segment (states-up-uk-hp) created st-up-assembly/st-uk-assembly with kind 'state_chamber' and older 2022-era partyStrength stats — this segment's entity patch uses kind 'state_legislature' per this segment's task instructions and CURRENT (2026-09-25) party-wise stats; the merge/build step should treat this as the newer record for stats and reconcile the kind field.

Left both positions in place (never invent by deleting a possibly-real legislator) but downgraded confidence high -> medium pending that check.

verification.method: Adversarial re-verification against LIVE sources (not memory): (1) validated JSON parse, ID-uniqueness, ID-rule pattern match (st-up-pos-mla-*/st-up-pos-mlc-*/st-uk-pos-mla-*), and vacant<->holder consistency programmatically -- 0 violations. (2) Fetched the live 'Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly' and 'Uttarakhand Legislative Assembly' Wikipedia articles fresh via the Wikipedia parse API (curl + bs4 raw HTML table parse, not WebFetch summarization) and diffed the CURRENT holder of all 403 UP + all 70 UK assembly seats against this file by seat number/constituency name -- full-population check, not a 30-sample spot-check. (3) Fetched the 'List of members of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council' Wikipedia article and filtered its 390-row historical roll to terms active as of 2026-09-25, then diffed holder names against this file's 99 filled UP MLC seats. (4) Checked the 'List of elections in India in 2026' Wikipedia article for any scheduled/held UP or UK by-elections not yet reflected here. (5) Recomputed party-wise strength stats directly from the 573 member records for all 3 chambers and compared to the entities[].stats blocks. (6) WebFetch spot-checks on individual holder pages for the one structural anomaly found (Mathura-Etah-Mainpuri MLC seat). Official state assembly portals (uplegisassembly.gov.in, uklegislativeassembly.gov.in) were unreachable this session (DNS/redirect failures) so could not be used directly; WebSearch quota (200/200) was exhausted before ECI-result cross-checks could be run, consistent with other segments in this research batch.
